title: the mountain ahead
hookLine: back to the battlefield: a warrior drops his bow, and the conversation begins
carry: you have the right to act. Not to the fruit

cards: Go back to day nine. A battlefield, two armies drawn up, conch shells blowing. Arjuna, a great archer, asks his charioteer to drive him out between the lines so he can see who he's about to fight.
He looks across and sees teachers, uncles, cousins, friends. His mouth goes dry. His bow slips from his hand.
And he sits down in the chariot and says he will not fight. We left him there, with his driver, Krishna, beside him. Today we find out what happens next.
Because the whole conversation that follows has a name, and it's the last word of this camp.

teach.h: THE SONG OF THE LORD, IN A CHARIOT.
teach.b: The Bhagavad Gita. The Song of the Lord. It sits inside the great epic, the Mahabharata, and it's a conversation between two people in a chariot.
On day nine you heard that the driver is Krishna, and a great deal more than a driver. Krishna does more than give orders. He teaches.
He talks about the self that cannot be killed, which you met as atman. He talks about acting without grabbing, about loving God, about seeing clearly. Look back at this week and you'll hear echoes.
Action with the self out of the way, the way seva works. Love as a path of its own, bhakti. The Gita holds these paths side by side.

teach.h: THE WHOLE CAMP IS IN THERE.
teach.b: Then the line this camp saved for last. In the second chapter Krishna says, in plain words: your right is to the action alone, never to its fruits. Don't let the fruit be your reason for acting.
And the verse keeps going: don't let that become a reason to do nothing, either. It isn't a way out of the fight.

teach.h: NOT A WAY OUT. A WAY TO STAND UP.
teach.b: It's a way to stand up and act without being owned by the result. And near the end of the Gita comes a surprise.
After everything, Krishna tells Arjuna to think it over fully, and then do as he chooses.

teach.h: YOU HAVE THE RIGHT TO ACT. NOT TO THE FRUIT.
teach.b: He hands the choice back. In the fourth camp you'll read this text itself, line by line. For now you get the door, and the sentence that opens it.

how: Hindus read and recite the Bhagavad Gita at home, in temples and in study groups, and some memorize its verses; its teaching on action without attachment to results is quoted in daily life.

games.q: BIG NEWS. Diya asked me to give a speech at her wedding 😱 what if i freeze and everyone hates it. should i just say no??
o: say yes. the speech is yours to give; how it lands isn't. Krishna says don't let fear of the result stop you acting.
say no. if it might go badly, it's safer not to try.
only say yes if you can promise it'll be perfect.
games.why: Arjuna dropped his bow, and Krishna taught him: your right is to the action, never to its fruit, and that's no reason to do nothing. Priya's part is the speech, not the applause.

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: drops his bow between the armies
the epic the Gita sits inside

s: the Gita is a separate book from the Mahabharata
it sits inside the great epic, a conversation in a chariot.
the Gita's line on the fruit of action means you can stop acting
Krishna says don't let it become a reason to do nothing. it's a way to stand up.
near the end, Krishna hands the choice back to Arjuna
think it over fully, he says, then do as you choose.

games.q: you're Krishna. your friend Arjuna has dropped his bow and says he won't fight. you've taught him everything. near the end, what do you tell him?
o: tell him to think it over fully, then choose.
games.why: near the end he hands the choice back: reflect on all of it, then do as you choose.

practice: Here's the practice: pick up the bow. Sit and breathe. Press your palms together at your chest, the way you did on day one.
Bring to mind one thing that's yours to do this week, the thing you've been sitting down in the chariot about. Picture doing it, fully. Then open your hand, and let go of how it turns out.
The action is yours. The fruit isn't. If you pray, you can offer the result to God.

wordCard.voice: The Gita. The Song of the Lord, a conversation in a chariot that gets a warrior back on his feet. Twenty-first word, and the door to the mountain.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the song (gita) of the Lord (bhagavat).

carryVoice: Your line: you have the right to act. Not to the fruit. Do one thing today that's yours to do, and let the result go. Tomorrow the stories begin, with a goddess, a bath, and a boy made of earth. Day twenty-one.

sources.ref: Bhagavad Gita 2.9 (Arjuna: I will not fight)
